epics.title: Runtime Observation & Launch Failure Remediation
epics.jtbd: When an automated verification harness executes post-clone runtime inspection, I want root docker-compose assets present and immediately discoverable, so that the runtime observation gate passes without launcher file-not-found errors.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Container launch success rate >= 99.9% without host port collision
epics.tocConstraintRef: docker-compose port binding conflict during runtime observation
requirements: R1: Configure docker-compose backend port binding with configurable host port or non-conflicting fallback variable to prevent 127.0.0.1:18080 bind collision during concurrent runtime observation harness runs

slices.title: Fix docker-compose backend host port binding collision in runtime observation stack
slices.jtbd: When implementing containerized runtime launch remediation for this epic, I want docker-compose.yml to support a configurable host port mapping (e.g. ${CRIE_BACKEND_PORT:-18080}) and clean container lifecycle flags, so that automated verification harnesses can launch the backend without 127.0.0.1:18080 port collision failures
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a host environment where port 18080 is already allocated,
When docker-compose is evaluated or executed with CRIE_BACKEND_PORT set to an alternate port,
Then the backend container successfully binds to the designated host port without socket collision;
Given docker-compose.yml in the repository root,
When inspecting service port definitions for the backend service,
Then the port specification uses an environment variable fallback syntax enabling flexible port assignment during automated observation.
slices.tocConstraintRef: host socket allocation constraint on port 18080
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero port-binding failures across 100 consecutive container initialization attempts
